text:
anya: Hi team, new hire here. I got the MacBook Air A1466 from ops. Setup mostly fine but a few snags: Docker won't start (says kernel extensions blocked), Homebrew asks to install Rosetta, and FileVault says it's already enabled but `fdesetup status` shows 'FileVault is Off'. Anyone seen this?

it_help: Welcome! Quick Qs: is that an Intel Air with T2? can you paste `system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep "Model Identifier"` and `system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep "Serial"`? Also screenshot of Docker error helps.

anya: Model Identifier: MacBookAir7,2
Serial: C02ABCDEF12
Docker error: "the system extension must be enabled in Security & Privacy".

devops: Sounds like our kernel extension whitelist didn't get accepted during OOBE. If MDM pushed the kext allowlist, you'd still need to click "Allow" in System Settings > Privacy & Security for some older macOS builds. Did you see a yellow banner at the top of Security & Privacy?

anya: I don't see a banner, but the Security pane is mostly locked; it asks for an admin to make changes. Also when I tried to install Homebrew it prompted to install Rosetta and failed because I wasn't admin.

it_help: We can do two things: 1) create temporary local admin so you can approve prompts and install Rosetta/Homebrew, or 2) we can push enterprise Rosetta + kext approvals remotely. Which do you prefer?

anya: I'd rather install a few dev tools myself if that's ok. Temp admin is fine.

it_help: Created temp admin `temp-anya` and sent password via DM. Use it only to approve system prompts and install tools. We'll expire it in 18 hours.

mac-deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Pushed MDM kext-approval profile for serial C02ABCDEF12 at 2026-04-02T09:01:05Z.

anya: Logged in as temp-anya, opened Security & Privacy, clicked "Allow" for developer network extensions. Docker started successfully after a restart.

anya: Ran `softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license` and then re-ran the Homebrew installer. Brew and `brew install awscli` work now.

devops: Great. About FileVault mismatch: our MDM sometimes pre-configures FileVault but the local `fdesetup` state can lag until the user logs in and the escrow agent completes. Can you run `sudo profiles status -type enrollment` and `fdesetup status` now and paste?

anya: `profiles status -type enrollment` -> shows the corporate MDM profile installed.
`fdesetup status` -> "FileVault is Off."

it_help: Ok, since MDM says it requested FileVault but it didn't finish, we can kick the escrow sequence. Running `sudo jamf enableFileVault` (for our tool) will attempt to enable and escrow recovery key non-interactively. Do you want us to run it, or would you rather enable via System Settings and keep the recovery key yourself?

anya: Run the jamf command please, I don't want to miss anything.

it_help: Running now.

mac-deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Request: run `sudo jamf enableFileVault` on C02ABCDEF12 at 2026-04-02T09:12:30Z.

it_help: Done. `fdesetup status` now shows "Encryption in progress" and we have an escrowed recovery key recorded to your device entry. Encryption will continue in the background; leave it plugged in overnight.

anya: Awesome, Docker + Homebrew working, FileVault encrypting. Thanks! One more small Q: VSCode keeps asking for kernel extension permission for our corporate dev helper. Is that part of the same kext approval?

devops: If it's a different vendor cert, we may need to push an additional approval or ask you to click Allow again in Privacy & Security. If it reappears, ping us and we'll widen the MDM approval list to include that vendor.

anya: Will do. Thanks for the quick assist :party_parrot:

it_help: Looping back: temp admin `temp-anya` will be deactivated in 18 hours. If you need it extended to finish anything, DM us.

mac-deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Device C02ABCDEF12: MDM profile & kext approvals applied; FileVault escrow complete at 2026-04-02T09:20:40Z.

anya: Thanks again, cheers!
